# SLAPorSLOP

> A store for open-source apps and games made with AI. Free to download or to play in the
> browser, checked before they're offered (the builds, or a browser game's address), rated by
> people who play them.

## Start here

- [Getting someone onto SLAPorSLOP](/start.md): for an AI assistant helping a person publish an app
  or offer their services on People, including people who have never used Git or GitHub: what to
  ask, what only the person can do, and how to make their first repository.

## Publishing

- [How to publish on SLAPorSLOP](/publishing.md): requirements, store pages, releases, Slop Build
  (GitHub Actions), maker signatures, Slop Pulse player counts (with code for Python, JS, Rust,
  Go, C# and Godot), where to keep saves (SLOP_SAVE_DIR, for sandbox mode), rules for online
  play and mods (copy them into your project's agent instructions), browser games (a game on
  your own website publishes an https play address instead of builds), dedicated servers (the
  Servers category), and a step-by-step checklist for agents. This one Markdown file is the
  whole guide; the page at /publish/guide shows the same text.

- Checks without an account: `/v1/check/store-address?slug=…`, `/v1/check/repository?url=…`,
  `/v1/check/portfolio?url=…` (GET, JSON with a `summary` first; dry runs, nothing saved).

## People

- [Your SLAPorSLOP portfolio](/portfolio.md): how creatives (artists, animators, composers, sound
  designers, writers…) build the portfolio their People page needs: the `.slop/portfolio.json`
  format, every limit SLAPorSLOP checks, ready-made templates, and a checklist for agents.

- Hiring someone on People: an assistant can write a maker's request with them and hand it over
  as one link to that creative's page (`/people/{handle}#fill=…`), which opens the hire form
  filled in for the person to check and send themselves. The fields are in /publishing.md, under
  "A link for hiring someone".

- Open requests: `GET /v1/work-requests` lists what makers say their projects need, newest first
  (tool `find_work_requests`). A request can be prepared as a link,
  `/people?view=requests#fill=…` (/publishing.md, "A link for an open request"); posting it is the
  person's to do.
